response.title: Can I charge a lithium trolling motor battery with the charger already built into my boat, or do I need to buy a new one?
response.answer:
You may be able to use your boat's existing onboard charger to charge a lithium trolling motor battery. It depends on the charger's model, charging profile, and the type of lithium battery.

If you're switching from traditional lead-acid or AGM batteries to lithium (usually LiFePO4), here's what you need to know.

When you can reuse your existing charger

Lithium-compatible charger: If your charger has a LiFePO4 or lithium charging mode, you're generally good to go.

Older lead-acid/AGM charger: Some can charge lithium batteries, but only if their voltage settings and charging behavior meet the battery manufacturer's requirements.

Charger with desulfation or equalization: These modes can produce voltages that are unsafe for lithium batteries. Don't use them unless the manufacturer explicitly approves the setup.

Automatic charger: Some older chargers won't recognize a lithium battery if its battery management system (BMS) has shut it down.

Typical charging voltages

Battery type

	

Typical charging voltage




12V LiFePO4

	

14.2–14.6V




24V LiFePO4

	

28.4–29.2V




36V LiFePO4

	

42.6–43.8V

These are common ranges, not universal requirements. Always follow your battery manufacturer's specifications.

What about a 2-bank or 3-bank onboard charger?

You can often keep using it if each bank provides the correct charging profile and voltage for the battery connected to it.

For example, a 3-bank onboard charger could charge three separate 12V lithium batteries in a 36V trolling motor system, provided the charger is designed for that arrangement and supports those batteries.

Let me check your specific setup

Tell me these three things:

Charger brand and model — for example, NOCO Genius GEN3, Minn Kota Precision, or ProMariner ProSport.

Lithium battery brand and model — or the battery you're thinking of buying.

Trolling motor voltage — 12V, 24V, or 36V.

With those details, I can tell you whether your existing charger is compatible, whether it has limitations, or whether you actually need to buy a new one.

Don't replace the charger yet. Many onboard chargers can work with lithium batteries, so it's worth checking first.
